Content:
Applying a row operation to any [MATH: 3\times 3] matrix is the same as pre-multiplying (multiplying on the left) the matrix by the corresponding elementary matrix.

Content:
For instance, if we wish to swap the first row and the second row of a [MATH: 3\times 3] matrix [MATH: A,] we pre-multiply [MATH: A] by the corresponding elementary matrix
[MATH: [0|1|0; 1|0|0; 0|0|1]]
to get [MATH: E_1 A.]

Content:
To perform a sequence of row operations to a [MATH: 3\times 3] matrix, we pre-multiply the matrix by the elementary matrix corresponding to the first operation, and then pre-multiply the result by the elementary matrix corresponding to the second operation.

Content:
For instance, given a [MATH: 3 \times 3] matrix [MATH: A,] suppose that we would like to multiply the second row by [MATH: 2] and then add [MATH: 3] times the first row to the second row. To do this, we first pre-multiply [MATH: A] by
[MATH: [1|0|0; 0|2|0; 0|0|1]]
to get [MATH: E_2 A.] Then we pre-multiply the result by
[MATH: [1|0|0; 3|1|0; 0|0|1]]
to get [MATH: E_3 E_2 A.]

[MATH: [1|0|0; 0|0|1; 0|1|0]]

Then, to apply the second elementary row operation to [MATH: E_1 A,] we multiply by [MATH: E_2] on the left and get [MATH: E_2 E_1 A\mathbin{:}]

[MATH: [6|0|0; 0|1|0; 0|0|1]]

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
Applying a row operation to any [MATH: 3\times 3] matrix is the same as pre-multiplying (multiplying on the left) the matrix by the corresponding elementary matrix.

Content:
For instance, if we wish to swap the first row and the second row of a [MATH: 3\times 3] matrix [MATH: A,] we pre-multiply [MATH: A] by the corresponding elementary matrix
[MATH: [0|1|0; 1|0|0; 0|0|1]]
to get [MATH: E_1 A.]

Content:
To perform a sequence of row operations to a [MATH: 3\times 3] matrix, we pre-multiply the matrix by the elementary matrix corresponding to the first operation, and then pre-multiply the result by the elementary matrix corresponding to the second operation.

Content:
For instance, given a [MATH: 3 \times 3] matrix [MATH: A,] suppose that we would like to multiply the second row by [MATH: 2] and then add [MATH: 3] times the first row to the second row. To do this, we first pre-multiply [MATH: A] by
[MATH: [1|0|0; 0|2|0; 0|0|1]]
to get [MATH: E_2 A.] Then we pre-multiply the result by
[MATH: [1|0|0; 3|1|0; 0|0|1]]
to get [MATH: E_3 E_2 A.]
